full: Extend this clip (attached) by 10 seconds, widescreen, silent, continuing directly from its last frame. For context, the clip was made from this story: A small neighbourhood barber shop on a quiet weekday afternoon: one black leather chair in front of a wide mirror with round bulbs, a worn wooden counter with clippers, combs and a talc brush, a striped pole outside the front window, warm tungsten light inside and soft daylight from the window. Marcus, the barber, mid-forties, shaved head, grey beard, black apron over a white t-shirt. Dev, the customer, early twenties, in the chair with a black cape, short dark hair being finished into a fade. What the clip showed: Marcus finishes the fade on Dev's right side with the clippers, steps back, tilts his head to check the line, then picks up the talc brush and dusts Dev's neck. Dev looks into the mirror. End on Marcus lifting the cape at Dev's shoulders, about to take it off. What happens next: Marcus pulls the cape off with a flick and shakes it out. Dev stands, runs a hand over the fresh fade in the mirror and grins. Marcus holds up a hand mirror behind Dev's head so he can see the back; Dev nods, satisfied. They shake hands by the counter. End on Dev turning toward the door, Marcus already brushing down the chair.
